finding: Migration uncertainty materially widens population uncertainty for Northern America.
implication_for_model: Do not interpret deterministic scenario differences as probability intervals.
correction_applied: Monte Carlo bands with arbitrary parameter distributions were removed from headline results.

study: Raftery & Ševčíková (2023, International Journal of Forecasting)
finding: Long-horizon population forecasts should be probabilistic and separately model fertility, mortality and migration.
implication_for_model: Report conditional scenarios and identification frontiers rather than a unique forecast.
correction_applied: China-like result is now a frontier and a zero-migration TFR interval.

finding: Turning points in fertility and net migration are major sources of U.S. projection error.
implication_for_model: Backtests and alternative component assumptions are required.
correction_applied: Results are reported under both Census and CBO fertility assumptions.

finding: Immigration can prevent population decline more readily than it can maintain support ratios; stabilizing aging requires implausibly large flows.
implication_for_model: Lower immigration should strongly affect population levels but only moderately affect aging ratios.
correction_applied: Counterfactual age-benchmark factors that exaggerated aging and decline were removed.

study: Ma et al. (2025, Population Research and Policy Review)
finding: Even very high immigration does not fully offset U.S. aging; immigration volume and composition strongly affect population and GDP.
implication_for_model: Age, nativity and skill composition matter; aggregate net migration is insufficient for fiscal inference.
correction_applied: Economic claims are limited to demographic mechanisms; fiscal effects are no longer inferred from dependency ratios alone.

study: Li et al. (2009, Journal of Population Research)
finding: China's aging is driven primarily by low fertility and mortality decline; migration has a small role.
implication_for_model: A U.S. China-like path requires East-Asian-level fertility, not merely immigration restrictions.
correction_applied: China-like TFR was recalibrated without CBO age-benchmark residuals.

finding: Long-run population size and dependency are highly sensitive to whether and when fertility rebounds.
implication_for_model: The convergence year must be shown explicitly.
correction_applied: Exact-fit results are reported for convergence in 2035, 2045, 2055 and 2070.
